draft.title: Gene flow and genetic drift
card: An allele frequency is how common an allele is in a population's gene pool, such as 30% of copies of a gene.
the movement of alleles between populations, when individuals or their gametes move from one population to another and breed. It can make two populations more alike.
a change in allele frequencies caused by chance, such as which individuals happen to survive and breed. It is not caused by an allele being more useful.
Drift has a much stronger effect in small populations. In a large population, chance events tend to average out. In a small one, an allele can be lost or become common quickly.
draft.remember: Gene flow moves alleles in. Drift changes frequencies by chance, most in small groups.

a.q: Pollen from a population of grevillea shrubs is carried by birds to a separate population, where it fertilises flowers. Which process does this describe?
opts: Gene flow
Genetic drift
Chromosomal mutation
Natural selection for a useful allele
a.why: Pollen carries alleles from one population into another, and the new seeds will carry them. That is gene flow. Genetic drift is a chance change in allele frequencies, not the movement of alleles between populations.
a.clue: Think about alleles crossing from one population to another.

b.q: A storm kills most of an island's 12 lizards at random. The few survivors, by chance, mostly carry a rare allele for green skin. Why did the allele become common?
opts: Genetic drift acted strongly on a small population
Green skin was a more useful trait for survival
Gene flow brought the allele in from another island
Green skin allele mutated in every surviving lizard
b.why: The deaths were random, and the survivors were few, so chance changed the allele frequency. That is genetic drift. Natural selection is the tempting answer, but the card says drift is not caused by an allele being more useful, and nothing here shows green skin helped survival.
b.clue: The storm killed at random, and the group was small.

b.best: Genetic drift acted strongly on a small population

problems.detail: "Gene flow moves alleles in" is narrower than the card, which defines gene flow as movement of alleles between populations. Gene flow also moves alleles out of a population. "Moves alleles between populations" would match the card.

check.summary: Both questions are sound, with one clear answer each, and the explanations match the card. The only issue is the remember line saying gene flow "moves alleles in" rather than between populations.
